It remains to compare (2) and (3). We use a form of the Cartan–Helgason criterion, spelled out in the Appendix. Let \(\pi\) satisfy (2). Since \(\pi\) is tempiric with regular infinitesimal character, it is equivalent with a standard representation 
\[ X_G(TA,{}^\backprime\Gamma,{}^\backprime \lambda,0) \] 
based on the fundamental Cartan subgroup $TA=Z_G(\mathfrak{l})$ where $\mathfrak{l}=Z_{\mathfrak{g}}(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q})$ for a compact Cartan subspace $\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}\subset \mathfrak{k}\cap \mathfrak{q}$, and \({}^\backprime\lambda\in i\mathfrak{t}^\ast\) is \(G\)-regular. Here, ${}^\backprime\lambda$ may not belong to $i\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}^*$. Let ${}^\backprime\Sigma_K^+={}^\backprime\Sigma^+(\mathfrak{k}^\mathbb{C},\mathfrak{t}^\mathbb{C})$, ${}^\backprime\Sigma_G^+={}^\backprime\Sigma^+(\mathfrak{g}^\mathbb{C},\mathfrak{t}^\mathbb{C})$ be the unique positive systems for which \({}^\backprime\lambda\) is dominant. Let ${}^\backprime\rho_K, {}^\backprime\rho_G$ be the corresponding half-sums of positive roots. Let \({}^\backprime\mathfrak{n}\) denote the sum of the positive root spaces in $\mathfrak{k}^\mathbb{C}$ determined by \({}^\backprime\Sigma_K^+\). Let ${}^\backprime T^l$ be the large Cartan subgroup of $K$ associated to ${}^\backprime\Sigma^+_K$.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:G-regular-standard-irreducible}, the standard representation $ X_G(TA,{}^\backprime\Gamma,{}^\backprime \lambda,0)$ is irreducible and has a unique lowest \(K\)-type \(\tau_\pi\). Moreover, the highest-weight representation of $
{}^\backprime T^l$ attached to $\tau_\pi$ is equivalent to the induced representation $\mathrm{Ind}_T^{{}^\backprime T^l}{}^\backprime \Gamma$.

Now, we choose a possibly different positive system  $\Sigma_{K}^{+}=\Sigma^+(\mathfrak{k}^\mathbb{C},\mathfrak{t}^\mathbb{C})$ that is (uniquely) compatible with some positive system $\Sigma_{c}^{+}=\Sigma^+(\mathfrak{k}^\mathbb{C},\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}^\mathbb{C})$. Consider $\mathfrak{n}$ and $T^{l}$ accordingly for this system. There is $w_0\in N_K(\mathfrak{t})$ such that $w_0\cdot {}^\backprime \Sigma^+_K = \Sigma^+_K$. By the previous part, the highest-weight representation $(\mu, W^\mathfrak{n})$ attached to $(\tau_\pi, W)$ with respect to this positive system is also an irreducible induced $T^{l}$-representation. Thus we have
\[
(\mu, W^\mathfrak{n})\cong \mathrm{Ind}_T^{T^l}\mathbb{C}_{\Gamma},
\]
where $\Gamma = w_0\cdot {}^\backprime \Gamma$. Note that $w_0\in N_K(\mathfrak{t}\oplus \mathfrak{a})$ automatically, and this implies $w_0\in N_K(T)$. Hence, $w_0$ conjugate $(TA, {}^\backprime \Gamma, {}^\backprime \lambda, 0)$ to   $(TA,  \Gamma, \lambda, 0)$ where $\lambda = w_0\cdot {}^\backprime \lambda$. 
Since $\Sigma_{K}^{+}$ is compatible with $\Sigma_{c}^{+}$,  Corollary~\ref{cor:appendix-parametrization} applies; therefore,
\[
\tau_\pi^{K\cap H}\neq0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\left(\operatorname{Ind}_T^{T^l}\mathbb{C}_\Gamma\right)^{T^l\cap H}\neq0.
\]

Since \(T\) is a normal subgroup of \(T^l\), we have 
\[
( \operatorname{Ind}^{T^l}_T \mathbb C_\Gamma)\mid_{T^l\cap H} \, 
\simeq
\bigoplus_{s\in (T^l\cap H)\backslash T^l/T}
\operatorname{Ind}^{T^l\cap H}_{(T^l\cap H)\cap T}\mathbb C_{s\Gamma}.
\]
Therefore there are nonzero \((T^l\cap H)\)-fixed vectors  if and only if
\((s\Gamma)|_{(T^l\cap H)\cap T}\) is trivial for some \(s\in T^l\), i.e.\ if and only if
\((s\Gamma)|_{T\cap H}=1\).

Replacing the character datum $(TA,  \Gamma, \lambda, 0)$ further by the equivalent \(s\)-conjugate datum, we
may therefore assume \(\Gamma|_{T\cap H}=1\). This implies that \(d\Gamma\)
vanishes on \(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{h}\) and $d\Gamma \in i\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}^*$.

Moreover, the corresponding root shifts \(\rho_G\) and \(\rho_K\) lie in \((\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast)^\mathbb{C}\): to see this, by Definition~\ref{def-character-datum-G} and Lemma~\ref{lem:rho-rho-eq}, we have
\[
d\Gamma + 2 \rho_K = \lambda + \rho_G 
\]
in $i\mathfrak{t}^*$. Compatibility of $\Sigma^+_K$ with $\Sigma^+_c$ implies $\rho_K\in i\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}^*$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem-minus-sigma}. Therefore, $\lambda + \rho_G\in i\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}^*$. The positive systems determined by $\lambda$ and $\lambda +\rho_G$ coincide. Therefore, $\lambda +\rho_G \in i\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}^*$ implies that $\rho_G\in i\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}^*$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem-minus-sigma}. 

Hence
\[
\lambda=d\Gamma-\rho_G+2\rho_K
\]
lies in \(i\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast\). This proves (2) \(\Rightarrow\) (3). 

Conversely, if $\pi$ satisfies (3), then $\pi$ is tempiric with regular infinitesimal character, and its unique lowest $K$-type $\tau_\pi$ is $K\cap H$-spherical by the argument above.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
\label{def:dataC}
A tempered \emph{character datum for \(X\)} is a quadruple
\((TA,\Gamma,\lambda,\nu)\) with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item \(TA\) is a \(\sigma\)-stable and \(\theta\)-stable Cartan subgroup of
\(G\), with Lie algebra
\[
\mathfrak{b}=\mathfrak{t}\oplus\mathfrak{a},
\qquad
\mathfrak{t}=\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{h}\oplus\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q},
\qquad
\mathfrak{a}=\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h}\oplus\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q},
\]
and
\[
\mathfrak{b}_\mathfrak{q}=\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}\oplus\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}
\]
is a Cartan subspace of \(\mathfrak{q}\);
\item \(\Gamma\) is a character of \(T\) such that
\[
\Gamma|_{T\cap H}=1;
\]
\item \(\lambda\in i\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast\), regarded as an element of \(i\mathfrak{t}^\ast\) after extending it by zero on \(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{h}\), is \(M'\)-regular, where
\[
M'A'=Z_G(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})
\]
is the Langlands decomposition of the centralizer of \(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}\);
\item \(\nu\in i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast\), regarded as an element of \(i\mathfrak{a}^\ast\) after extending it  by zero on \(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h}\);
\item the differential of \(\Gamma\) satisfies
\[
d\Gamma=
\lambda+\rho_{\mathfrak{m}'}-2\rho_{\mathfrak{m}'\cap\mathfrak{k}}
\qquad\text{in }i\mathfrak{t}^\ast.
\]
Here the positive systems defining \(\rho_{\mathfrak{m}'}\) and
\(\rho_{\mathfrak{m}'\cap\mathfrak{k}}\) are the ones for which \(\lambda\) is dominant and
regular on \(\mathfrak{m}'\).
\end{enumerate}
Omitting \(\nu\), we call \((TA,\Gamma,\lambda)\) a \emph{discrete character
datum for \(X\)}. We call $i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast$ the \emph{relative continuous parameter space} for the  datum $(TA, \Gamma, \lambda)$, and $i\mathfrak{a}^\ast$ the \emph{full continuous parameter space}.
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:rho_rho_eq}
Let \((TA,\Gamma,\lambda,\nu)\) be a character datum for \(X\). Let
\[
MA=Z_G(\mathfrak{a})
\]
be the Langlands decomposition of the centralizer of the full split part
\(\mathfrak{a}\). Then \(\lambda\) is \(M\)-regular and
\[
\rho_{\mathfrak{m}'}-2\rho_{\mathfrak{m}'\cap\mathfrak{k}}
=
\rho_{\mathfrak{m}}-2\rho_{\mathfrak{m}\cap\mathfrak{k}}
\]
in \(i\mathfrak{t}^\ast\). Consequently \((TA,\Gamma,\lambda,\nu)\), with \(\nu\)
extended by zero on \(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h}\), is a character datum for \(G\).
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Since \(\mathfrak{m}\subset\mathfrak{m}'\), \(M'\)-regularity of \(\lambda\) implies
\(M\)-regularity. Inside the reductive group \(M'\), the relevant Cartan subgroup is
\(T\exp(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h} \cap \mathfrak{m}')\). Its split part is \(\exp(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h} \cap \mathfrak{m}')\), and \(M\) is the Levi
subgroup obtained by centralizing this split part. Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:rho-rho-eq} inside \(M'\) gives the displayed
identity. Consequently, the defining differential relation for a character
datum of \(X\) in Definition~\ref{def:dataC}\textup{(5)} becomes the
defining differential relation for a character datum of \(G\) in Definition~\ref{def-character-datum-G}.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- theorem-15: body_md -->
\label{thm:tempered spec}
Let \(X=G/H\) be a well-tempered symmetric space, and suppose that \(G\) is
a real reductive linear group in Vogan's class. Let \(\pi\in\widehat G\) be an
irreducible unitary representation of \(G\). Then \(\pi\) belongs to
\(\operatorname{supp}(\lambda_X)\) if and only if \(\pi\) is equivalent to an
irreducible constituent of \(X_G(TA,\Gamma,\lambda,\nu)\), where \((TA,\Gamma,\lambda,\nu)\) is a character datum for the symmetric space \(X\).
<!-- end theorem-15 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Suppose first that \((TA,\Gamma,\lambda,\nu)\) is a character datum for
\(X\). Let
\[
M'A'=Z_G(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}),
\]
and let \(P'=M'A'N'\) be a cuspidal \(\sigma\)-parabolic subgroup with this
Levi factor. By Lemma~\ref{lem:welltemp_hereditary}, the smaller symmetric
space
\[
M'/(M'\cap H)
\]
is well-tempered. It has discrete series because \(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}\) is a compact Cartan
subspace of \(\mathfrak{m}'\cap\mathfrak{q}\). Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:ds_para} to
\(M'/(M'\cap H)\), with Cartan subgroup \(T\exp(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h} \cap \mathfrak{m}')\subset M'\), together with Lemma \ref{lem:G-regular-standard-irreducible}, shows
that the standard representation
\[
\xi= X_{M'}(T\exp(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h} \cap \mathfrak{m}'),\Gamma,\lambda,0)
\]
is irreducible and belongs to \(\widehat{M'}_{M'\cap H,\mathrm{ds}}\). By induction in
stages, the standard representation
\(X_G(TA,\Gamma,\lambda,\nu)\) is 
\[
\operatorname{Ind}_{P'}^G(\xi\otimes e^\nu\otimes 1).
\]
Here \(\nu\in i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast\) is viewed as a unitary character of \(A'\) by extension by zero on the remaining split directions $\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h}'$. Hence
every irreducible constituent of the standard representation \(X_G(TA,\Gamma,\lambda,\nu)\) belongs to
\(\operatorname{supp}(\lambda_X)\) by Theorem~\ref{thm_description}.

Conversely, let \(\pi\in\operatorname{supp}(\lambda_X)\). By
Theorem~\ref{thm_description}, there exist a \(\theta\)-stable Cartan
subspace \(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}\oplus\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}\subset\mathfrak{q}\), a cuspidal \(\sigma\)-parabolic subgroup
\[
P'=M'A'N',
\qquad
M'A'=Z_G(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}),
\]
a  representation of~$M'$ in the discrete spectrum
\[
\xi\in\widehat{M'}_{M'\cap H,\mathrm{ds}},
\]
and \(\nu\in i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast\), such that \(\pi\) is an irreducible constituent of
\[
\operatorname{Ind}_{P'}^G(\xi\otimes e^\nu\otimes1).
\]
The symmetric space \(M'/(M'\cap H)\) is well-tempered by
Lemma~\ref{lem:welltemp_hereditary} and has discrete series. Therefore
Theorem~\ref{thm:ds_para}, applied to \(M'/(M'\cap H)\), gives a discrete
character datum \((T\exp(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h} \cap \mathfrak{m}'),\Gamma,\lambda)\) for \(M'\) such that
\[
\xi \cong X_{M'}(T\exp(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h}\cap \mathfrak{m}'),\Gamma,\lambda,0),
\]
with \(\Gamma|_{T\cap H}=1\) and with \(\lambda\in i\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast\) \(M'\)-regular.
Adjoining the split factor \(\exp(\mathfrak{a}')\) and keeping the same
\(\nu\in i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast\), we obtain a character datum
\[
(TA,\Gamma,\lambda,\nu)
\]
for \(X\), and the induced representation above is
\(X_G(TA,\Gamma,\lambda,\nu)\).
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- blank-10: body_md -->
Recall from Theorem~\ref{thm:HC_disjoint} that the connected components of \(\widehat G_{\mathrm{temp},\mathrm{Haus}}\) are in natural bijection with the set $\mathcal{C}_G$ of   \(K\)-conjugacy classes
\([TA,\Gamma,\lambda]\) of discrete character data for \(G\). If \(c\) is an element of $\mathcal{C}_G$, with discrete character datum representative \((TA,\Gamma,\lambda)\), the corresponding connected component \(\widehat G_{\mathrm{temp},\mathrm{Haus}}(c)\) of \(\widehat G_{\mathrm{temp},\mathrm{Haus}}\)  has the form 
\[
i\mathfrak{a}^\ast/W(\Gamma,\lambda)
\]
where $\mathfrak{a}$ is the (real) Lie algebra of~$A$, and $W(\Gamma, \lambda)$ is the finite group in Notation~\ref{notation-w}.
 We have also seen that every discrete character datum \(D\)
for \(X\) (Definition \ref{def:dataC})  defines, after certain extensions by zero, a discrete
character datum for \(G\): see Lemma~\ref{lem:rho_rho_eq}.
<!-- end blank-10 -->
<!-- blank-11: body_md -->
\label{def:CX-and-DX}
Let \(\mathcal D_X\) be the set of discrete character data for \(X\). We say that two discrete character data $(T_1A_1,\Gamma_1,\lambda_1)$ and $(T_2A_2,\Gamma_2,\lambda_2)$ for $X$ are \emph{$\sigma$-conjugate} if there is $k\in K$ such that 
\[
\mathrm{Ad}_k (T_1A_1, \Gamma_1, \lambda_1) = (T_2A_2, \Gamma_2, \lambda_2) \,\, \text{and} \,\,  \mathrm{Ad}_k({\mathfrak{a}_1}_\mathfrak{q})={\mathfrak{a}_2}_\mathfrak{q}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal D_X / {\sim_\sigma}\) be the set of $\sigma$-conjugacy classes $[TA,\Gamma,\lambda]_\sigma$ of discrete character data for \(X\). If
\(D=(TA,\Gamma,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_X\), write
\[
[D]_G=[TA,\Gamma,\lambda]\in\mathcal C_G
\]
for the corresponding $K$-conjugacy class of discrete character data for $G$.  The map 
\begin{align*} \kappa\colon\quad  \mathcal{D}_X & \to \mathcal{C}_G\\ 
D & \mapsto  [D]_G
\end{align*}
descends to a map
\[
\overline{\kappa}\colon\quad  \mathcal{D}_X /{\sim_\sigma} \to \mathcal C_G.
\]
The latter map $\overline{\kappa}$ is finite-to-one, but not injective in general. 

Let $\mathcal{C}_X \subset \mathcal{C}_G$ be the image of $\kappa$, and for $c \in \mathcal{C}_X$, let $\mathcal{D}_X(c)$ be the fiber of $\kappa$ over~$c$, i.e. $\mathcal{D}_X(c) =  \{ D \in \mathcal{D}_X  \ : \ [D]_G = c\}$.

The intersection \( \mathrm{supp}(\lambda_X)_{\mathrm{Haus}} \cap \widehat G_{\mathrm{temp},\mathrm{Haus}}(c)\) is a single connected component of \(\mathrm{supp}(\lambda_X)_{\mathrm{Haus}} \). We shall see that if we identify  \(\widehat G_{\mathrm{temp},\mathrm{Haus}}(c)\) with  \(i\mathfrak{a}^\ast/W(\Gamma,\lambda)\), the corresponding component of \(\mathrm{supp}(\lambda_X)_{\mathrm{Haus}}\)  can be described as the image in \( i\mathfrak{a}^\ast/W(\Gamma,\lambda)\) of a finite (explicit) union of linear subspaces of~$i\mathfrak{a}^\ast$.
<!-- end blank-11 -->
<!-- notation-2: body_md -->
Fix \(c\in\mathcal C_X\) and $D_0= (TA,\Gamma,\lambda)\in \mathcal D_X(c)$.

Write
\[
\mathfrak{b}=\mathfrak{t}\oplus\mathfrak{a},
\qquad
\mathfrak{t}=\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{h}\oplus\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q},
\qquad
\mathfrak{a}=\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h}\oplus\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q},
\]
for the corresponding \(\sigma\)-decompositions, and put
\[
V_\mathfrak{q}:=i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast\subset i\mathfrak{a}^\ast.
\]
Let $W(\lambda)$ and $
W(\Gamma,\lambda)$ be as in Notation~\ref{notation-w}, so that 
\(\widehat G_{\mathrm{temp},\mathrm{Haus}}(c)\) is homeomorphic to $
i\mathfrak{a}^\ast/W(\Gamma,\lambda)$.The group $W(\lambda)$ acts on $i\mathfrak{a}^\ast$, and we let $W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)$ be the global stabilizer of the subspace $V_\mathfrak{q}$ for that action:
\[
W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)
=
\{u\in W(\lambda):u(V_\mathfrak{q})=V_\mathfrak{q}\}.
\]
<!-- end notation-2 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:weak-weyl-normal-form}
Let \(D\in\mathcal D_X(c)\). Choose a \(K\)-conjugacy carrying the
discrete character datum for \(G\) underlying \(D\) to
\(D_0=(TA,\Gamma,\lambda)\), and use it to identify the full continuous
parameter space attached to \(D\) with the fixed space \(i\mathfrak{a}^\ast\).
Under this identification, the image of the relative continuous parameter
space attached to \(D\) has the form
\[
w^{-1}V_\mathfrak{q}\subset i\mathfrak{a}^\ast
\]
for some \(w\in W(\lambda)\). The resulting class of \(w\) in
\[
W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)\backslash W(\lambda)/W(\Gamma,\lambda)
\]
depends only on the $\sigma$-conjugacy class $[D]_\sigma \in \mathcal{D}_X/{\sim_\sigma}$, and not on the choice of $K$-conjugacy or the choice of $w$.
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Write \(D=(T_DA_D,\Gamma_D,\lambda_D)\), and choose \(k\in K\)
such that \(kD=D_0\) as discrete character data for \(G\).  By adjusting
\(k\) on the left by a representative of an element
\(w\in W(\lambda)\), we can arrange that $g:=wk$ carries the \(\sigma\)-eigenspace decomposition of
\(\operatorname{Lie}(T_DA_D)\) to the $\sigma$-eigenspace  decomposition of \(\mathfrak{b}\). To see this, since $Z_{\mathfrak{g}^\lambda}(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})$ is abelian, a generic element in $\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}$ determines a positive system $\Sigma^+(\mathfrak{g}^\lambda, \mathfrak{a})$ such that $\sigma(\Sigma^+(\mathfrak{g}^\lambda, \mathfrak{a}))= - \Sigma^+(\mathfrak{g}^\lambda, \mathfrak{a})$. Choose $\Sigma^+(\mathfrak{g}^{\lambda_D}, \mathfrak{a}_D)$ similarly. Then, there is $w\in  W(\lambda)$ so that $g=wk$ carries $\Sigma^+(\mathfrak{g}^\lambda, \mathfrak{a})$ to $\Sigma^+(\mathfrak{g}^{\lambda_D}, \mathfrak{a}_D)$. This, together with $(wk)\cdot \lambda_D = \lambda$, implies $\mathrm{Ad}_g$ and $\mathrm{Ad}_{\sigma(g)} =\sigma(\mathrm{Ad}_g)$ coincide as maps from $\mathfrak{t}_D\oplus \mathfrak{a}_D$ to $\mathfrak{t} \oplus \mathfrak{a}$. Hence, $\mathrm{Ad}_g$ respects the $\sigma$-eigenspace decompositions. We also have \(gD=wD_0\).  Since \(g\) carries the source relative continuous
parameter subspace to \(V_\mathfrak{q}\), transport by \(k=w^{-1}g\) carries it
to \(w^{-1}V_\mathfrak{q}\).

Suppose that \(k_iD=D_0\) and that
\(g_i=w_i k_i\), for \(i=1,2\), are two such eigenspace-preserving
transports.  The Weyl class of \(k_2k_1^{-1}\) lies in
\(W(\Gamma,\lambda)\), because this element stabilizes \(D_0\).
The Weyl class of \(g_2g_1^{-1}\) lies in \(W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)\), because
this element preserves the fixed relative parameter subspace.  Since
\[
g_2g_1^{-1}
=
w_2(k_2k_1^{-1})w_1^{-1},
\]
the elements \(w_1\) and \(w_2\) lie in the same
\(W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)\)--\(W(\Gamma,\lambda)\) double coset. 

Given $D\in \mathcal{D}_X(c)$ and $g=wk$ as above, if $D=k'D'$ for $D' \in \mathcal{D}_X(c)$ where $k'\in K$ preserves relative continuous parameter spaces, $g'=wkk'$ sends $D'$ to $D_0$ preserving the $\sigma$-eigenspace decomposition of the relevant Cartan subspaces for $D'$ and $D_0$. Hence, the resulting class of $w$ depends only on the $\sigma$-conjugacy class of $D$.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- definition-14: body_md -->
\label{def:branch-set}
The set of \emph{branch-indexing double cosets} for in the component of \(\widehat G_{\mathrm{temp},\mathrm{Haus}}(c)\), relative to the fixed representative $D_0=(TA,\Gamma,\lambda)\in \mathcal{D}_X(c)$, is the subset
\[
\operatorname{Br}_X(D_0)
\subseteq
W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)\backslash W(\lambda)/W(\Gamma,\lambda)
\]
consisting of the double-coset classes produced by
Lemma~\ref{lem:weak-weyl-normal-form} as \(D\) ranges over
\(\mathcal D_X(c)\).
Let $\mathcal B_X(D_0)$ be a subset of $W(\lambda)$ which contains one representative for each double coset in $\operatorname{Br}_X(D_0)$. Define a subset $\Sigma_X(D_0)$ of $i\mathfrak{a}^\ast/W(\Gamma,\lambda)$ by
\[
\Sigma_X(D_0)
=
\left(
\bigcup_{w\in\mathcal B_X(D_0)} w^{-1}V_\mathfrak{q}
\right)\Big/ W(\Gamma,\lambda).
\]
In other words, \(\Sigma_X(D_0)\) is the union, over
\([w]\in\operatorname{Br}_X(D_0)\), of the images of 
\(w^{-1}V_\mathfrak{q}\) in \(i\mathfrak{a}^\ast/W(\Gamma,\lambda)\). We may call these images the ``branches'' of \(\Sigma_X(D_0)\).

Let $\Sigma_X(c)$ be the subset of the connected component $\widehat G_{\mathrm{temp},\mathrm{Haus}}(c)$ that corresponds to \(\Sigma_X(D_0)\) under the identification $G_{\mathrm{temp},\mathrm{Haus}}(c)\simeq i\mathfrak{a}^\ast/W(\Gamma,\lambda)$.
<!-- end definition-14 -->
<!-- theorem-16: body_md -->
\label{thm:shape-practical}
Let \(X=G/H\) be a well-tempered symmetric space, and assume that \(G\) is
in Vogan's class.   
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The image of \(\operatorname{supp}(\lambda_X)\)
in the Hausdorff quotient \(\widehat G_{\mathrm{temp},\mathrm{Haus}}\) is
\[
\operatorname{supp}(\lambda_X)_{\mathrm{Haus}}
\cong
\bigsqcup_{c\in\mathcal C_X}\Sigma_X(c).
\]
\item For each \(c\in\mathcal C_X\), choose a representative $D_0 \in \mathcal{D}_X(c)$; then the subset
\(\Sigma_X(D_0)\) is a finite union of the images of the linear subspaces
\(w^{-1}V_\mathfrak{q}\subset i\mathfrak{a}^\ast\) in 
\(i\mathfrak{a}^\ast/W(\Gamma,\lambda)\). Thus $\Sigma_X(c)$ is connected. 
\item 
In particular, the connected components of $\operatorname{supp}(\lambda_X)_{\mathrm{Haus}}$ are the sets $\Sigma_X(c)$, for $c \in \mathcal{C}_X$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-16 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{thm:tempered spec}, the support is the union of the
irreducible constituents of standard representations attached to character
data for \(X\). The Vogan parametrization for \(G\) in
Theorem~\ref{thm:HC_disjoint} identifies the component of
\(\widehat G_{\mathrm{temp},\mathrm{Haus}}\) indexed by \(c=[D_0]_G\) with
\[
i\mathfrak{a}^\ast/W(\Gamma,\lambda).
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:weak-weyl-normal-form}, for each \(D\in\mathcal D_X(c)\), the relative continuous parameter
space of \(D\) contributes to this component the image of
\(w^{-1}V_\mathfrak{q}\) for some \(w\in W(\lambda)\), where the double-coset class $W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)wW(\Gamma,\lambda)$ is determined by $D$. Taking the union
over all \(D\in\mathcal D_X(c)\) gives exactly \(\Sigma_X(D_0)\).  Finally, taking the disjoint union over \(c\in\mathcal C_X\) gives the asserted image of the support in the Hausdorff quotient.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor_singleton}
Let $X=G/H$ be a well-tempered symmetric space, and assume $G$ is in Vogan's class. A representation in $\mathrm{supp}(\lambda_X)$ belongs to the discrete series of $X$ if and only if it is an isolated point of $\mathrm{supp}(\lambda_X)$.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{thm:shape-practical}, the component of
\(\operatorname{supp}(\lambda_X)_{\mathrm{Haus}}\) indexed by a discrete character datum 
\([TA,\Gamma,\lambda]\) for $X$ is the image of a finite union of linear
subspaces \(w^{-1}(i\mathfrak a_{\mathfrak q}^\ast)\), all containing
\(0\). It is a singleton exactly when
\(\mathfrak a_{\mathfrak q}=0\).

If \(\mathfrak a_{\mathfrak q}\neq0\), continuity of parabolic
induction shows that each constituent over a given parameter is a
Fell limit of constituents over nearby relative parameters, and
therefore is not isolated. If
\(\mathfrak a_{\mathfrak q}=0\), the inducing
\(\sigma\)-parabolic is \(G\) itself, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:G-regular-standard-irreducible} shows that the
corresponding standard representation is irreducible. Its component
is therefore a single isolated representation. These are precisely the discrete-series representations of
\(X\).
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:regular-branch-stabilizer}
Let \(w\in W(\lambda)\).  If
\[
w(V_\mathfrak{q}^{\mathrm{reg},\lambda})\cap V_\mathfrak{q}^{\mathrm{reg},\lambda}
\neq\varnothing,
\]
then \(w\in W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)\).
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
We give the argument on \(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}\), using the invariant inner product to pass
between \(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}\) and \(i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast\).  Choose a representative
\(n\in N_K(\mathfrak{b})\) of \(w\), and suppose that
\(Y\in\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^{\mathrm{reg},\lambda}\) and \(\operatorname{Ad}(n)Y\in\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^{\mathrm{reg},\lambda}\).
Since \(Y,\operatorname{Ad}(n)Y\in\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}\), both are in the
\((-1)\)-eigenspace of \(\sigma\). Moreover,
\(\sigma\circ\operatorname{Ad}(n)=\operatorname{Ad}(\sigma(n))\circ\sigma\). Therefore
\[
-\operatorname{Ad}(n)Y
=
\sigma(\operatorname{Ad}(n)Y)
=
\operatorname{Ad}(\sigma(n))\sigma(Y)
=
-\operatorname{Ad}(\sigma(n))Y.
\]
It follows that
\(\operatorname{Ad}(n)Y=\operatorname{Ad}(\sigma(n))Y\). Applying
\(\operatorname{Ad}(\sigma(n)^{-1})\) to this equality gives
\[
\operatorname{Ad}(\sigma(n)^{-1}n)Y=Y.
\]
The element \(\sigma(n)^{-1}n\) represents an element of the Weyl group of
\(\mathfrak{g}^\lambda\), and it fixes the regular element \(Y\).  Since $Y$ is regular, its Weyl-group stabilizer in \(\mathfrak{g}^\lambda\) is trivial.  Thus
\(\sigma(n)^{-1}n\) acts trivially on \(\mathfrak{b}\).  Consequently, \(\operatorname{Ad}(n)\) and \(\operatorname{Ad}(\sigma(n))\) have the same action on
\(\mathfrak{b}\). Hence, for every \(Z\in\mathfrak{b}\),
\[
\sigma(\operatorname{Ad}(n)Z)
=
\operatorname{Ad}(\sigma(n))\sigma(Z)
=
\operatorname{Ad}(n)\sigma(Z),
\]
where the last equality uses \(\sigma(Z)\in\mathfrak{b}\). Thus \(\operatorname{Ad}(n)\)
commutes with \(\sigma\) on~\(\mathfrak{b}\). It follows that \(\operatorname{Ad}(n)\) preserves the
\(\sigma\)-eigenspace decomposition of \(\mathfrak{a}\), in particular
\(\operatorname{Ad}(n)\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}=\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}\).  Hence \(w(V_\mathfrak{q})=V_\mathfrak{q}\), i.e.\ \(w\in W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)\).
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:generic-branch-separation}
Let \(w_1,w_2\in W(\lambda)\).  If the images of
\(w_1^{-1}V_\mathfrak{q}^{\mathrm{reg},\lambda}\) and
\(w_2^{-1}V_\mathfrak{q}^{\mathrm{reg},\lambda}\) in
\(i\mathfrak{a}^\ast/W(\Gamma,\lambda)\) intersect, then
\[
W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)w_1W(\Gamma,\lambda)
=
W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)w_2W(\Gamma,\lambda).
\]
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
If the images meet, then for some \(u\in W(\Gamma,\lambda)\) and some
\(\nu_1,\nu_2\in V_\mathfrak{q}^{\mathrm{reg},\lambda}\),
\[
\nu_2=w_2u w_1^{-1}\nu_1.
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:regular-branch-stabilizer}, the element
\(w_2u w_1^{-1}\) belongs to \(W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)\).  Thus, $w_1$ and $w_2$ belong to the same double coset.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
\label{rem:branch-intersections}
All branches contain the image of
\(0\), and they may meet along singular lower-dimensional strata.  The
preceding proposition says that this is the only possible kind of overlap:
distinct branch labels have disjoint regular parts.  Example \ref{subsec_example_SL3} below exhibits two branch images whose union has three one-dimensional arms meeting at one point.
<!-- end remark-8 -->
<!-- definition-15: body_md -->
\label{def:admissible-w}
Let \(D_0=(TA,\Gamma,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_X(c)\).  Set
\[
\mathcal A_X^{\mathrm{sc}}(D_0)
=
\{w\in W(\lambda):(TA,w\Gamma,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_X\}.
\]
and 
\[
\operatorname{Br}^{\mathrm{sc}}_X(D_0)
:=
\{W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)wW(\Gamma,\lambda):w\in
\mathcal A_X^{\mathrm{sc}}(D_0)\}.
\]
<!-- end definition-15 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:same-cartan-weyl-form}
The inclusion $\operatorname{Br}^{\mathrm{sc}}_X(D_0) \subset \operatorname{Br}_X(D_0)$ holds for any $D_0$. Furthermore, 
if $\operatorname{Br}^{\mathrm{sc}}_X(D_0)=\operatorname{Br}_X(D_0)$, then
\[
\Sigma_X(D_0)
=
\left(
\bigcup_{w\in\mathcal A_X^{\mathrm{sc}}(D_0)} w^{-1}V_\mathfrak{q}
\right)\Big/ W(\Gamma,\lambda).
\]
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
If \(w\in\mathcal A_X^{\mathrm{sc}}(D_0)\), then
\((TA,w\Gamma,\lambda)\) is itself a discrete character datum for~$X$ whose discrete class for \(G\) is
\(c=[D_0]_G\). Its relative continuous parameter space is
\(V_\mathfrak{q}=i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast\). Transporting its underlying datum for \(G\) back to the representative \(D_0\) by a representative of \(w^{-1}\) sends this parameter space to
\(w^{-1}V_\mathfrak{q}\).  This proves that its double-coset class belongs to
\(\operatorname{Br}_X(D_0)\).  The final formula follows immediately if all
branch classes are represented in this way.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:same-cartan} Suppose $H=G^\sigma$. Then for any discrete character datum $D_0=(TA, \Gamma, \lambda)$ for $X$, we have $\operatorname{Br}^{\mathrm{sc}}_X(D_0)=\operatorname{Br}_X(D_0)$. Thus, 
\[
\Sigma_X(D_0)
=
\left(
\bigcup_{w\in\mathcal A_X^{\mathrm{sc}}(D_0)} w^{-1}V_\mathfrak{q}
\right)\Big/ W(\Gamma,\lambda).
\]
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
By the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:weak-weyl-normal-form}, for any $w\in\operatorname{Br}_X(D_0)$ there are $k\in K$ and a discrete character datum $D=(T_DA_D, \Gamma_D, \lambda_D)$ for $X$ with the property $(wk)\cdot D=w\cdot D_0 = (TA,w\Gamma,\lambda)$ where $wk$ maps $\mathfrak{t}_D\oplus \mathfrak{a}_D$ to $\mathfrak{t}\oplus \mathfrak{a}$ preserving the $\sigma$-eigenspaces. Thus $\mathrm{Ad}_{wk}\colon \mathfrak{t}_D\oplus \mathfrak{a}_D \to \mathfrak{t}\oplus \mathfrak{a}$ coincides with $\sigma(\mathrm{Ad}_{wk})=\mathrm{Ad}_{\sigma(wk)}$. It follows that $\sigma(wk)\cdot (wk)^{-1} \in Z_K(\mathfrak{t}\oplus \mathfrak{a})=T$. Thus $\sigma(wk)=zwk$ for some $z\in T$. Using this, we can see that \[ \sigma(\mathrm{Ad}_{wk}(T_D \cap G^{\sigma})) = \mathrm{Ad}_{zwk}(T_D \cap G^{\sigma}) = \mathrm{Ad}_{wk}(T_D \cap G^{\sigma});\] therefore, $\mathrm{Ad}_{wk}(T_D \cap G^{\sigma}) \subset T\cap G^\sigma$. Similarly, $\mathrm{Ad}_{(wk)^{-1}}(T \cap G^{\sigma}) \subset T_D\cap G^\sigma$. These imply $\mathrm{Ad}_{wk}(T_D \cap G^{\sigma}) = T\cap G^\sigma$. 

Since $\Gamma_D$ is trivial on $T_D\cap G^{\sigma}$, $w\cdot \Gamma = (wk)\cdot \Gamma_D$ is trivial on $T\cap G^\sigma$. Thus, $(TA, w\Gamma, \lambda)=w\cdot (TA, \Gamma,\lambda) = (wk)\cdot (T_DA_D, \Gamma_D, \lambda_D)$ is a discrete character datum for $X$. Here, we used the assumption $H=G^\sigma$. The first assertion follows from this. The second assertion follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:same-cartan-weyl-form}.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:branch-collapse}
Suppose that
\[
W(\lambda)=W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)W(\Gamma,\lambda).
\]
Then $\operatorname{Br}_X(D_0)$ consists of just the identity coset $
\{W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)W(\Gamma,\lambda)\}$,
and
\[
\Sigma_X(D_0)
=
\operatorname{image}
\bigl(V_\mathfrak{q}\longrightarrow i\mathfrak{a}^\ast/W(\Gamma,\lambda)\bigr).
\]
In particular, the subspaces \(w^{-1}V_\mathfrak{q}\), for
\(w\in W(\lambda)\), all have the same image in the component
\(i\mathfrak{a}^\ast/W(\Gamma,\lambda)\) of
\(\widehat G_{\mathrm{temp},\mathrm{Haus}}\).
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
The displayed factorization says exactly that
\(W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)\backslash W(\lambda)/W(\Gamma,\lambda)\) is a
singleton.  The datum \(D_0\) contributes this class, so the branch set is
the displayed singleton.  Equivalently, if \(w=uv\) with
\(u\in W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)\) and \(v\in W(\Gamma,\lambda)\), then
\[
w^{-1}V_\mathfrak{q}=v^{-1}u^{-1}V_\mathfrak{q}=v^{-1}V_\mathfrak{q},
\]
which has the same image as \(V_\mathfrak{q}\) in
\(i\mathfrak{a}^\ast/W(\Gamma,\lambda)\).  The formula for \(\Sigma_X(D_0)\)
follows.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- remark-9: body_md -->
\label{rem:when-same-cartan-simplifies}
The factorization hypothesis of Proposition~\ref{prop:branch-collapse}
holds in particular if either
\(W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)=W(\lambda)\) or
\(W(\Gamma,\lambda)=W(\lambda)\). If $\lambda$ is $G$-regular, both conditions hold. 

The first case, \(W_\mathfrak{q}(\lambda)=W(\lambda)\), occurs for instance  when
\(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}=\mathfrak{a}\) or \(0\). These two limiting cases are useful to keep in mind. If \(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}=\mathfrak{a}\), then \(V_\mathfrak{q}=i\mathfrak{a}^\ast\), and
\(\Sigma_X(D_0)\) is the entire component
\(i\mathfrak{a}^\ast/W(\Gamma,\lambda)\) of
\(\widehat G_{\mathrm{temp},\mathrm{Haus}}\). If \(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}=0\), then we have
\(V_\mathfrak{q}=\{0\}\), and the corresponding connected component
\(\Sigma_X(D_0)\) of
\(\operatorname{supp}(\lambda_X)_{\mathrm{Haus}}\) is a point.

The second case \(W(\Gamma,\lambda)=W(\lambda)\) is the situation which will occur when we turn to spaces of type $G_\mathbb C/G_\mathbb R$ in  Section~\ref{sec:complex}: the relevant Cartan
subgroups are connected, so the character \(\Gamma\) is determined by its
differential, and any element which stabilizes \(\lambda\) also stabilizes \(\Gamma\).
<!-- end remark-9 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:relative-Weyl} The restriction of the quotient map $q_\lambda$ \eqref{eq:qlambda} to $i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^*$ descends to
\[
\overline{q_\lambda} \colon i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^*/W^\sigma(\lambda) \to  i\mathfrak{a}^*/W(\lambda).
\]
The map $\overline{q_\lambda}$ is injective; therefore, the image of $i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^*$ under $q_\lambda$ is canonically homeomorphic to $i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^*/W^\sigma(\lambda)$.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
Since $W^\sigma(\lambda)\subset W(\lambda)$ preserves $i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^*$, $q_\lambda\mid_{i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^*}\colon i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^*\to i\mathfrak{a}^* /W(\lambda)$ descends to $\overline{q_\lambda} \colon i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^*/W^\sigma(\lambda) \to  i\mathfrak{a}^*/W(\lambda)$. We show that this map is injective. Let $\mathfrak{g}^{\lambda}=Z_\mathfrak{g}(\lambda)$. We note that $Z_{\mathfrak{g}^{\lambda}}(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})=\mathfrak{b}$ since $\lambda$ is $M'$-regular where we recall $M'A'=Z_G(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})$. Below, we identify $i\mathfrak{a}^*$ with $\mathfrak{a}$ using an invariant metric.

Without loss of generality, we show the injectivity in the case when $\lambda=0$ and $Z_{\mathfrak{g}}(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})=\mathfrak{b}$. This reduction can be made by working inside the semisimple part of $\mathfrak{g}^{\lambda}$ after splitting off the center of $\mathfrak{g}^{\lambda}$ on which $W(\lambda)$ acts trivially. 

Let $W=W(\mathfrak{t}\oplus \mathfrak{a})$ and let $W^\sigma=W(\mathfrak{t}\oplus \mathfrak{a})^\sigma$. We fix compatible positive systems $\Sigma^+(\mathfrak{g}, \mathfrak{a})$, $\Sigma^+(\mathfrak{g}, \mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})$. By $Z_\mathfrak{g}(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})=\mathfrak{b}$, for any root  $(\alpha, \beta)\in \mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h}^*\oplus \mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^*$, we have $\beta\neq0$. Thus, the root is positive if and only if $\beta \in  \Sigma^+(\mathfrak{g}, \mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})$. Let $\mathfrak{a}^{++}\subset \mathfrak{a}$ be the dominant closed Weyl chamber. The compatibility between our positive systems implies that $\mathfrak{a}^{++}\cap \mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q} = \mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^{++}$ is the dominant closed Weyl chamber for the restricted, possibly non-reduced, root system $\Sigma(\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})$. Since $\mathfrak{a}^{++}$ is a fundamental domain of the $W$-action on $\mathfrak{a}$, we may identify $i\mathfrak{a}^*/W$ with $\mathfrak{a}^{++}$. By \cite[Theorem~5]{Rossmann79}, which applies since $\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}$ is maximal abelian in $\mathfrak{p} \cap \mathfrak{q}$ under the assumption $Z_\mathfrak{g}(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})=\mathfrak{b}$, the Weyl group of the possibly non-reduced root system $\Sigma(\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})$ is $W_K(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})$ and thus $i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^*/W_K(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})$ identifies with $\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^{++}$. Moreover, the action of $W^{\sigma}$ on~$\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^*$ factors through the surjection $W^{\sigma} \to W_K(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})$: the map is surjective since for any $w\in N_K(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})$, our assumption that  $Z_\mathfrak{g}(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})=\mathfrak{b}$ implies that $w\in N_K(\mathfrak{a})$. Hence, we have canonical identifications $i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^*/W^\sigma \cong i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^*/W_K(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}) \cong \mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^{++}$ under which the map $\overline{q_\lambda}$ identifies with the embedding $\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^{++}\to \mathfrak{a}^{++}$,  proving the injectivity. The homeomorphism claim follows since the topological embedding $\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^{++}\to \mathfrak{a}^{++}$ is a~homeomorphism onto its image.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- theorem-17: body_md -->
\label{thm:GcGr-main}
Let \(X=G/H\) be a symmetric space of type \(G_{\mathbb C}/G_{\mathbb R}\).
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item \(X\) is well-tempered.

\item For every \(\theta\)-stable Cartan subalgebra
\(\mathfrak{b}_\mathfrak{h}=\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{h}\oplus\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h}\subset\mathfrak{h}\), and for every discrete character datum
\((TA,\Gamma,\lambda)\) for \(X\) based on
\(TA=Z_G(\mathfrak{b}_\mathfrak{h}\oplus i\mathfrak{b}_\mathfrak{h})\), the map
\[
 i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast/W^\sigma(\lambda)
 \longrightarrow \widehat G_{\mathrm{temp}},
 \qquad
 \overline\nu\longmapsto X_G(TA,\Gamma,\lambda,\nu),
\]
is a homeomorphism onto its image.  Denote this image by
$
\widehat X_{\mathfrak{b}_\mathfrak{h},\lambda}
$.
The support of the Plancherel measure is the disjoint union
\[
\mathrm{supp}(\lambda_X)
=
\bigsqcup_{[\mathfrak{b}_\mathfrak{h}]}
\ \bigsqcup_{[(\Gamma,\lambda)]}
\widehat X_{\mathfrak{b}_\mathfrak{h},\lambda},
\]
where \([\mathfrak{b}_\mathfrak{h}]\) runs over the \(K\)-conjugacy classes of \(\theta\)-stable
Cartan subalgebras of \(\mathfrak{h}\), and \([(\Gamma,\lambda)]\) runs over the
\(W^\sigma(\mathfrak{b}_\mathfrak{h})\)-orbits of discrete character data for \(X\) based on
\(TA=Z_G(\mathfrak{b}_\mathfrak{h}\oplus i\mathfrak{b}_\mathfrak{h})\).

\item \(X\) has discrete series if and only if the real Lie algebra \(\mathfrak{h}\) is
split.  In that case the discrete series of \(X\) is precisely the set of
representations
\[
X_G(TA,\Gamma,\lambda,0)
\]
attached to split Cartan subalgebras of \(\mathfrak{h}\) and to the corresponding
discrete character data for \(X\).  It coincides with the set of tempiric
representations of \(G\) with regular infinitesimal character whose unique
lowest \(K\)-type is \(K\cap H\)-spherical.

\item A representation in \(\mathrm{supp}(\lambda_X)\) belongs to the discrete series
of \(X\) if and only if it is an isolated point of \(\mathrm{supp}(\lambda_X)\).
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-17 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
Part~(1) is Example~\ref{ex:GcGr-welltemp}.

For part~(2), Theorem~\ref{thm:tempered spec} identifies
\(\mathrm{supp}(\lambda_X)\) with the union of the tempered standard representations
attached to character data for \(X\). By the discussion above,
\(W(\Gamma,\lambda)=W(\lambda)\). Let
\[
q_\lambda:i\mathfrak{a}^\ast\longrightarrow i\mathfrak{a}^\ast/W(\lambda)
\]
be the quotient map. Proposition~\ref{prop:branch-collapse} collapses the
branch union in the component of
\(\widehat G_{\mathrm{temp},\mathrm{Haus}}\) indexed by
\([TA,\Gamma,\lambda]\) to
\[
q_\lambda(i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast) \cong i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast/W^\sigma(\lambda),
\]
where the homeomorphism is by Lemma~\ref{lem:relative-Weyl}. 

By Wallach's irreducibility theorem and Vogan's parametrization, this
homeomorphism corresponds precisely to the map
\[
\overline\nu\longmapsto X_G(TA,\Gamma,\lambda,\nu).
\]
Re-indexing
Cartan data by \(K\)-conjugacy classes of \(\theta\)-stable Cartan subalgebras
\(\mathfrak{b}_\mathfrak{h}\subset\mathfrak{h}\) gives the stated disjoint decomposition.

For part~(3), Theorem~\ref{thm:equal-rank} says that \(X\) has discrete series
if and only if \(\mathfrak{q}\) contains a compact Cartan subspace.  In the present
setting compact Cartan subspaces of \(\mathfrak{q}=i\mathfrak{h}\) are precisely the subspaces
\[
\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}=i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h},
\]
where \(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h}\) is a split Cartan subalgebra of \(\mathfrak{h}\).  Thus \(X\) has
discrete series if and only if \(\mathfrak{h}\) is split.  Once this is known, the
characterization of the discrete series is Theorem~\ref{thm:ds_para}
specialized to the present class of symmetric spaces.

Part~(4) is the content of Corollary~\ref{cor_singleton}.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- remark-10: body_md -->
Although all Cartan subgroups of the complex group $G$ are conjugate under
$G$, the support decomposition in Theorem~\ref{thm:GcGr-main}(2) is indexed by
$K$-conjugacy classes of Cartan subalgebras of the real form $\mathfrak{h}$, or
 equivalently by $K$-conjugacy classes of Cartan subspaces of $\mathfrak{q}$.
<!-- end remark-10 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
\label{cor:GcGr-Cstar}
With the notation of Theorem~\ref{thm:GcGr-main}, there is a canonical
isomorphism
\[
C^*_{\lambda_X}(G)
\cong
\bigoplus_{[\mathfrak{b}_\mathfrak{h}]}
\ \bigoplus_{[(\Gamma,\lambda)]}
C_0\bigl(i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast/W^\sigma(\lambda),\mathfrak{K}\bigr).
\]
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
For connected complex semisimple groups, the block decomposition of
\(C_r^*(G)\) into trivial homogeneous algebras over the tempered parameter
spaces is due to Penington--Plymen \cite{PP83}; it is also recovered from the
\(C^*\)-algebraic parabolic-induction framework in
\cite{CCH16,CHS24,CHST24}. The $C^\ast$-algebra  \(C^*_{\lambda_X}(G)\) identifies with the quotient of $C^\ast_r(G)$ by the annihilator of the unitary representation of $C^\ast_r(G)$ determined by $\lambda_X$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:GcGr-main}(2), the spectrum
of the quotient \(C^*_{\lambda_X}(G)\) of $C^*_r(G)$ is the closed Hausdorff subspace
\(\mathrm{supp}(\lambda_X)\) of $\widehat{G}_\mathrm{temp}$, whose connected pieces are the spaces
\(i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast/W^\sigma(\lambda)\).  Passing to the quotient
\(C^*_{\lambda_X}(G)\) restricts the block functions to this closed subspace,
which gives the displayed direct sum.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{thm_K_GcGr}
Let \(X=G/H\) be a symmetric space of type \(G_{\mathbb C}/G_{\mathbb R}\).
Then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item \(K_\ast(C^*_{\lambda_X}(G))\neq 0\);
\item for a Cartan subspace \(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}\subset\mathfrak{k}\cap\mathfrak{q}\), equivalently for every
such Cartan subspace, \(Z_\mathfrak{k}(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q})\) is abelian;
\item for a Cartan subspace \(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h}\subset\mathfrak{p}\cap\mathfrak{h}\), equivalently for every
such Cartan subspace, \(Z_\mathfrak{h}(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h})\) is abelian;
\item the real Lie algebra \(\mathfrak{h}\) is quasi-split.
\end{enumerate}
If these conditions hold, and if \(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}\oplus\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}\) is the most compact Cartan
subspace of \(\mathfrak{q}\), then
\[
K_\ast(C^*_{\lambda_X}(G))
\cong
\begin{cases}
\bigoplus_{\widehat K_{K\cap H,\mathrm{reg}}}\mathbb{Z},
& \ast\equiv \dim(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})\pmod 2,\\[1ex]
0,
& \ast\equiv \dim(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})+1\pmod 2.
\end{cases}
\]
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
By Proposition~\ref{cor:GcGr-Cstar}, the \(K\)-theory is the direct sum of the topological \(K\)-theories of the quotient spaces
\(i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast/W^\sigma(\lambda)\).  For the Weyl-group quotients
appearing here, a summand contributes trivially to $K$-theory when the
stabilizer \(W^\sigma(\lambda)\) acts non-trivially on $i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast$. To see this, using the notations from the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:relative-Weyl}, by splitting $\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}$ as $\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^1\oplus \mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^0$ where $\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^0$ is the intersection of $\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}$ with the center of $\mathfrak{g}^{\lambda}$ on which $W(\lambda)$ acts trivially, $i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast/W^\sigma(\lambda)$ is identified as the product of $\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^0$ and the closed dominant Weyl chamber $\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^{1,++}$ of $\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^1$ for the possibly non-reduced root system $\Sigma(\mathfrak{g}^{\lambda}, \mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^1)$. The system is non-empty; therefore, for the half-sum $\rho$ of the positive roots, translation by $t\rho$ for $t\geq0$ shows that $C_0(i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^{*}/W^\sigma(\lambda))\cong C_0(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^0)\otimes C_0(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^{1,++})$ is contractible (homotopic to the zero $C^*$-algebra).

On the other hand, a summand contributes non-trivially when the
stabilizer \(W^\sigma(\lambda)\) acts trivially on \(i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q}^\ast\); in
that case the contribution is \(\mathbb{Z}\) in parity \(\dim(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{q})\). These summands correspond exactly to the regular \(K\cap H\)-spherical lowest \(K\)-types.  Their
existence is equivalent to the existence of an element of \(\mathfrak{k}\cap\mathfrak{q}\) which
is regular in \(\mathfrak{g}\), or equivalently to \(Z_\mathfrak{k}(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q})\) being abelian for a
Cartan subspace \(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}\subset\mathfrak{k}\cap\mathfrak{q}\).  Under the correspondence
\(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}=i\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h}\), this is equivalent to \(Z_\mathfrak{h}(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h})\) being abelian for a Cartan
subspace \(\mathfrak{a}_\mathfrak{h}\subset\mathfrak{p}\cap\mathfrak{h}\).  For a real semisimple Lie algebra this is
the standard quasi-split condition.  This proves the equivalences and the
stated degree shift.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{prop:appendix-connected-CH}
Assume that $K$ and $H$ are connected.  Let $(\pi,V)$ be an irreducible
finite-dimensional representation of $K$, and let
$\lambda\in X^*(T_0)$ be its highest weight with respect to~$\Delta^+$.  Then
\[
V^H\neq 0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\lambda|_{T_0\cap H}=1.
\]
If these equivalent conditions hold, then $\dim_\mathbb{C} V^H=1$, and the averaging
operator
\[
P_H(v):=\int_H \pi(h)v\,dh
\]
is nonzero on the highest weight line.
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
This is the compact Cartan--Helgason theorem; see
\cite[Theorem~4.1 and Corollary~4.2]{helgason}.  For the torus formulation used here, namely the criterion
\(\lambda|_{T_0\cap H}=1\), see also \cite[Theorem 12.3.13]{GoodmanWallach}.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- remark-11: body_md -->
\label{rem:appendix-TcapH-disconnected}
Even when $H$ is connected, the subgroup $T_0\cap H$ need not be connected.
Thus the condition \(\lambda|_{T_0\cap H}=1\) in Proposition~\ref{prop:appendix-connected-CH} is genuinely stronger than the
infinitesimal condition $d\lambda|_{\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{h}}=0$.
<!-- end remark-11 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
\label{prop:appendix-connected-H}
Assume that $H$ is connected, but allow $K$ to be disconnected.  Let
$(\pi,V)$ be an irreducible finite-dimensional representation of~$K$.  Then the
averaging operator over $H$ restricts to an isomorphism
\[
P_H : (V^\mathfrak{n})^{T^l\cap H}\xrightarrow{\sim} V^H.
\]
Hence,
\[
\dim_\mathbb{C} V^H=\dim_\mathbb{C} (V^\mathfrak{n})^{T^l\cap H}.
\]
In particular, $V$ is $H$-spherical if and only if the dominant representation
$V^\mathfrak{n}$ contains the trivial representation of $T^l\cap H$.
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Since $H$ is connected, one has $H\subset K_0$.  Moreover $T^l\cap K_0=T_0$,
and therefore
$
T^l\cap H=T_0\cap H$.


Decompose $V$ as a finite direct sum $\bigoplus_{j=1}^N V_j$ of irreducible $K_0$-modules. 
Then
\[
V^\mathfrak{n}=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N V_j^\mathfrak{n},
\qquad
V^H=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N V_j^H.
\]
For each $j$, Proposition~\ref{prop:appendix-connected-CH} shows that
\[
P_H:(V_j^\mathfrak{n})^{T_0\cap H}\longrightarrow V_j^H
\]
is an isomorphism.
Summing over $j$, we see that $
P_H:(V^\mathfrak{n})^{T_0\cap H}\xrightarrow{\sim} V^H$ is an isomorphism. 
Since $T^l\cap H=T_0\cap H$, this is exactly the required statement.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:appendix-components}
$H=H_0\,(T^l\cap H).$
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Set
\[
M':=Z_H(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}),
\qquad
M_H^l:=N_H(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q},\Sigma^+),
\]
and let \(M'_0\) denote the identity component of \(M'\).

We first show that \(H=H_0M_H^l\). It is enough to prove that $H \subset H_0 M_H^l$. 
Let $h\in H$.  Since $\operatorname{Ad}(h)\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}$ is maximal abelian in $\mathfrak{q}$,
there exists $h_1\in H_0$ such that
\[
\operatorname{Ad}(h_1h)\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}=\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}.
\]
Thus $h_1h\in N_H(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q})$.  The restricted Weyl group
\[
W(\mathfrak{k},\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q})=N_{H_0}(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q})/Z_{H_0}(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q})
\]
acts transitively on the Weyl chambers of
$\Sigma(\mathfrak{k}^\mathbb{C},\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}^\mathbb{C})$, so there exists
$n\in N_{H_0}(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q})$ such that
\[
\operatorname{Ad}(nh_1h)\Sigma^+=\Sigma^+.
\]
Hence $nh_1h\in M_H^l$, and this concludes the proof that $
H=H_0\,M_H^l$.

Now let $m\in M_H^l$.  Since $m$ preserves $\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}$, it normalizes
$Z_{\mathfrak{h}}(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q})=\mathfrak{m}'$.  Therefore $\operatorname{Ad}(m)\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{h}$ is a maximal abelian
subspace of $Z_{\mathfrak{h}}(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q})$.  By conjugacy of maximal tori in the connected
compact group $M'_0$, there exists $m_1\in M'_0$ such that
\[
\operatorname{Ad}(m_1m)\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{h}=\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{h}.
\]
Thus $m_1m$ normalizes $\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{h}$.  The Weyl group
\[
W(M'_0,\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{h})=N_{M'_0}(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{h})/Z_{M'_0}(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{h})
\]
acts transitively on the Weyl chambers of the root system
$\Delta_0=\{\alpha\in \Delta(\mathfrak{k}^\mathbb{C},\mathfrak{t}^\mathbb{C}):\alpha|_{\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}}=0\}$, so there
exists $n_1\in N_{M'_0}(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{h})$ such that
\[
\operatorname{Ad}(n_1m_1m)\Delta_0^+=\Delta_0^+,
\]
where
$
\Delta_0^+:=\{\alpha\in \Delta^+:\alpha|_{\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}}=0\}$.
Set
\[
x:=n_1m_1m.
\]
Because \(n_1,m_1\in M'_0\subset Z_H(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q})\), both these elements centralize \(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}\) and hence preserve \(\Sigma^+\). Since $m\in M_H^l$, this element also preserves $(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q},\Sigma^+)$.
Thus $x$ preserves $(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q},\Sigma^+)$.  By construction, $x$ also preserves
$(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{h},\Delta_0^+)$.  Since the full positive system $\Delta^+$ is compatible
with $\Sigma^+$, these two facts imply that $x$ preserves the pair
$(\mathfrak{t},\Delta^+)$.  Equivalently,
\[
x\in N_K(\mathfrak{t},\Delta^+)\cap H=T^l\cap H.
\]
As $n_1m_1\in M'_0$, we obtain
$m\in M'_0\,(T^l\cap H)$.
This proves 
\[
M_H^l\subset M'_0\,(T^l\cap H).
\]

The reverse inclusion is clear: $M'_0$ centralizes $\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q}$, hence lies in
$M_H^l$, and every element of $T^l\cap H$ preserves $(\mathfrak{t},\Delta^+)$, in
particular preserves $(\mathfrak{t}_\mathfrak{q},\Sigma^+)$.  Therefore
\[
M_H^l=M'_0\,(T^l\cap H).
\]
Combining this with $H=H_0M_H^l$ gives $
H=H_0\,(T^l\cap H)$.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:appendix-general}
Let $K$ be a compact Lie group, let $H$ be an open subgroup of~$K^\sigma$, and
let $(\pi,V)$ be an irreducible finite-dimensional representation of~$K$.
Then the averaging map over $H_0$ induces an isomorphism of
$T^l\cap H$-modules
\[
P_{H_0}:(V^\mathfrak{n})^{T_0\cap H_0}\xrightarrow{\sim} V^{H_0}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
V^H \simeq (V^\mathfrak{n})^{T^l\cap H},
\qquad
\dim_\mathbb{C} V^H=\dim_\mathbb{C} (V^\mathfrak{n})^{T^l\cap H}.
\]
In particular, $V$ is $H$-spherical if and only if the dominant representation
$V^\mathfrak{n}$ contains the trivial representation of $T^l\cap H$.
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:appendix-connected-H} to the connected subgroup
$H_0$.  This gives a $T^l\cap H$-equivariant isomorphism
\[
P_{H_0}:(V^\mathfrak{n})^{T^l\cap H_0}\xrightarrow{\sim} V^{H_0}.
\]
The equivariance follows because every element of $T^l\cap H$ normalizes both
$H_0$ and the Borel subalgebra $\mathfrak{b}$.

Moreover, by Lemma~\ref{lem:appendix-components} we have
 $
H=H_0\,(T^l\cap H)
$, hence
\[
V^H=(V^{H_0})^{T^l\cap H}.
\]
Taking $T^l\cap H$-fixed vectors in the isomorphism above, we obtain
\[
V^H
\simeq
\bigl((V^\mathfrak{n})^{T^l\cap H_0}\bigr)^{T^l\cap H}
=
(V^\mathfrak{n})^{T^l\cap H},
\]
because $T^l\cap H_0\subset T^l\cap H$.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{cor:appendix-parametrization}
Under Vogan's highest-weight classification \cite[Theorem 1.17]{VoganUnitaryBook} for possibly disconnected compact
groups, the assignment
\[
(\pi,V)\longmapsto V^\mathfrak{n}
\]
restricts to a bijection between \(H\)-spherical irreducible representations
of \(K\) and dominant irreducible representations \((\mu, V_\mu)\) of \(T^l\) satisfying
\(V_\mu^{T^l\cap H}\neq0\).

If $\pi$ and $\mu$ are matched by that bijection, then 
\[
\dim_\mathbb{C} V^H=\dim_\mathbb{C} V_\mu^{T^l\cap H}.
\]
When $K$ is connected, $\mu$ is a character of $T_0$, and the condition above
reduces to
\[
\mu|_{T_0\cap H}=1.
\]
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
This is immediate from Proposition~\ref{prop:appendix-general}.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- remark-12: body_md -->
Let \(K\) be a product of finitely many copies of \(O(2)\). Then
\(\mathfrak k^\mathbb C\) is abelian, so the chosen Borel subalgebra is
\(\mathfrak b=\mathfrak k^\mathbb C\), and hence
\[
T^l=N_K(\mathfrak b)=K.
\]
In this case Corollary~\ref{cor:appendix-parametrization} is tautological.
<!-- end remark-12 -->
